title: Montenegro celebrates European Heritage Award for Pacijenca Project – Safeguarding the Dobrota Lace Tradition
content:
On 25 September, the Pacijenca Project – Safeguarding the Dobrota Lace Tradition, a 2026 European Heritage Award / Europa Nostra Award winner, was celebrated with a moving event at St. Tryphon Cathedral in Kotor, Montenegro. “Pacijenca” is the second Montenegrin project to receive Europe’s top heritage award in nearly 25 years. The ceremony, held as part of the European Heritage Days, brought together national and municipal officials, representatives of cultural institutions, the lace-making community led by Nada Radović, and the wider public.

Led by Museums of Kotor, the Pacijenca Project was awarded in the Education, Training and Skills category for reviving the endangered skill of Dobrota needle lace-making through sustained teaching, public demonstrations and contemporary heritage interpretation. Its name comes from the Italian word for patience, “pazienza”.

title: Denmark focuses on building favourable preconditions for Action Plan implementation
content:
On 28 September, Denmark hosted the first official meeting of the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region National Coordinators Group. This meeting, followed by a full working day with a wider stakeholder group, marked the kick-off of the Danish Presidency 2026-2027.

Denmark’s Presidency of the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region focuses on:

  • Ensuring an effective start to the implementation phase of the updated Action Plan (2026, pending European Commission approval). The Presidency encourages Policy Areas to use the first implementation phase to prepare the ground for their Actions to be taken forward across the Baltic Sea Region, including by identifying relevant partners, funding opportunities, and cooperation links with programmes, organisations, and actors in the region.
  • Increased Ukrainian involvement in the Strategy where relevant.
    The Presidency encourages Policy Areas and Steering Groups to take Ukraine into account when planning their work and to consider relevant opportunities for involving Ukrainian actors in Actions and cooperation activities.

title: Living better while living longer
content:
Europeans are living longer. This is one of the achievements of our social model. The question is whether we are living those additional years in good physical and mental health and whether this progress is shared equally across society.

The pursuit of longevity cannot simply mean adding years to life. It just as well means adding life to those years. In other words, extending the time in which we can take a full part in society, keep our relationships, feel accomplished and live with dignity. Importantly, though, healthy longevity must not become another privilege that correlates with income or social status. The right to healthy longevity needs to become an imperative of the progressive agenda for Europe.

title: Kuvataiteen tilastot 2025 on julkaistu
content:
Suomalaisten taidemuseoiden ja taidegallerioiden käyntimäärät pysyivät korkealla tasolla vuonna 2025. Vuodentakainen kävijäennätys ylittyi jälleen, kertoo Framen julkaisema kymmenes kuvataiteen vuositilasto. Kuvataidekohteiden käyntimäärät ovat nousseet 40 prosenttia vuosikymmenen aikana. Viime vuonna kuvataidetapahtumien käyntimäärä nousi merkittävästi erityisesti suosittujen valotaidetapahtumien myötä.

Suomalaisiin kuvataidekohteisiin – taidemuseoihin, taidegallerioihin ja kuvataidetapahtumiin – tehtiin kaikkiaan yli 5,3 miljoonaa käyntiä vuonna 2025. Kävijämäärä nousi hieman edellisvuoden ennätyslukemista. Tieto selviää Frame Contemporary Art Finlandin julkaisemista kuvataiteen tilastoista. Vuositilasto on järjestyksessään kymmenes.

Rovaniemen taidemuseo oli lähes 100 000 kävijällään toiseksi suosituin taidemuseokohde pääkaupunkiseudun ulkopuolella vuonna 2025. Kuva Reidar Särestöniemen näyttelystä Sukuni juuret ovat yöauringon maassa (24.1-1.6.2025). Kuva: Tatu Kantomaa

title: In Brazil’s capital, residents grow their own heat-fighting solutions
content:
Following a national pattern, Brasília concentrates green spaces in the most affluent areas

Originally published on Global Voices

Nasaré Francisca da Silva waters crops at Floresta da Nasaré, in Ceilândia, Brazil, where her agroforestry project emerged from a rubbish tip. Photo by Fabio Pozzebom/Dialogue Earth, used with permission.

This story by Lobato Felizola was originally published on Dialogue Earth’s website on July 14, 2026. It is republished here under a partnership agreement with Global Voices, with edits. It’s also part of Dialogue Earth’s work on the Community Adaptations to City Heat (CATCH) project, in partnership with Boston University.

Brasília was designed to be a green city. Tree planting was so central to planning for the Brazilian capital that it was described as a park city. This is evident in its central area, with cool, tree-lined avenues and green parks where locals enjoy walks. The city was built in just 41 months, replacing the savanna-type biome Cerrado with a gleaming new capital.

title: How do you know when AI is wrong? Lessons from our AI x Investigative Journalism Forum
content:
Your story's data came from a scraper a reporter vibe-coded. The spot checks came back clean. Do you publish?

We opened the AI x Investigative Journalism Forum at The New York Times on Sept. 25 with that question, and 81% of attendees said they'd hold the story until someone reviewed the code. On the live polling app I built for the kickoff, attendees dragged a dot toward their answer, and 70% of the "hold" voters pushed theirs nearly all the way to the edge.

It was a snap judgment, made on phones in seconds. Reading the code is part of checking such a tool, but it won't tell you how often the output is wrong. For that, several speakers argued, you have to test the results.

That afternoon, Avery Schmitz of CNN taught attendees to vibe-code their own flight-tracking analysis and closed the workshop with his own stricter rule: "Never vibe code to a finding," and a checklist to go with it: check every finding against the raw source, reproduce the key claim and read the lines of code that produce it.

title: America, the Threatened?
content:
By Jonathan Power

LUND, Sweden | 30 September 2026 (IDN) — The French ambassador to the US from 1902 to 1924, Jean-Jules Jusserand, observed that distant powers could not easily threaten the US because “On the north, she has a weak neighbour; on the south, another weak neighbour; on the east, fish and on the west, fish”.

The coming of the submarine-based nuclear missile has not changed that. Apart from the fact that no enemy would dare use them for fear of retaliation, and that there is no country in the world that feels that hostile to America (except North Korea), the fact is America is too big and too far away to be invaded and dominated. A foreign army could not launch a blitzkrieg across the Midwest or create a Vichy America.

The real tragedy of 9/11 is that, just as a majority of the US electorate had settled into a post-Cold War comfort zone, with the new president, George W. Bush, not being overly pushy or confrontational in foreign affairs, America was jolted so badly that a large proportion of its electorate has been paranoid ever since.
